title: Measuring contract damages
question: What does the injured party get, and where does the law stop?

steps.note: Consequential damages only when foreseeable at contracting.
Substantial performance; diminution in value when the cost to cure is grossly out of proportion.
No recovery for costs run up after the other side repudiates.
Cost of completion even when it dwarfs the increase in land value.
Diminution for the misplaced wall; cost of repair for the rest.
Diminution in value when restoration is incidental and cost is grossly disproportionate.
Mitigation requires only comparable substitute employment.
